To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we prove that the gradient of the potential is inLq, for allq>2, in a bounded, simply connected NTA-domain inR2.
we proved the integrability of the Green potential in a bounded NTA-domain in terms of a reverse Höelder inequality for the Green potential.
in a bounded, connected NTD-domain Ω⊂Rn, n≥2, the Green potential Gf of a function f∈Lq(Ω), 1≤q≤n/(n−1), is in W1,Lq(Ω) provided that the domain Ω satisfies the reverse Hölder condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the question: how much regularity can we expect from solutions of Poisson’s equation in domains with a fractal boundary?
the following question: what is the best exponent for the Lq-inequalities in the case of bounded NTA-domains?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results are valid for any bounded NTA-domain inRn,n=2,3,..., for which the reverse Hölder inequality holds for the Green function.
our results are valid for any domain inRn,n ≥ 2, for which the Green function satisfies a reverse Hölder condition close to the boundary and for which the boundary is not too badly non-rectifiable.
the integrability of (Gf) depends on the integrability of the Green function and on the geometry of the boundary of the domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proved that in the plane, the Green potential (or the Poisson kernel) of a bounded simply connected NTD-domain is in L2, if and only if its boundary has finite length.
we prove the validity of the Sobolev embedding theorem in the setting of bounded, connected NATA domains with a highly irregular boundary.

we prove that the Green potentials in bounded, connected, NTA-domains are in the space W1,ploc for allp∈ (1,∞) and that this is the optimal result in the sense that the Green potential is not in the space W12loc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Green potential (and the solution to Poisson's equation with a Lq-source term) is integrable in the Lq-sense for all exponentsq∈(1,∞).
the Green potential is integrable in Lq-classes for allq∈(1,∞) in domains with a quasidifferentiable boundary.
the validity of reverse Hölder inequalities for Green functions in NTA-domains is equivalent to the integrability of the Green potentials.
